backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same radius-2 Morgan generator (keep 2048 bits). Counts of each substructure carry more information than presence bits. Keep the RandomForest settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute MACCS structural keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, 167 bits) for each molecule and concatenate them to the 2048-bit Morgan vector before fitting the RandomForest. MACCS keys encode pharmacophore-like substructures that the Morgan bits miss.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys to the Morgan features

backlog.spec: Compute all RDKit 2D descriptors (rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors, about 200 values) for each molecule, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip extreme values to the 0.1 and 99.9 percentiles of the training set, and concatenate them to the Morgan bits. Fit the same RandomForest. BBB penetration depends strongly on properties like TPSA, MW, logP and H-bond counts.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physicochemical descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the fingerprint with about 12 physicochemical features: Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, formal charge, fraction sp3, heavy atom count, count of carboxylic acid groups, and count of basic amines. Fit a RandomForest with min_samples_leaf=3 on these features. Low-dimensional features may generalize better across unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Small interpretable physchem feature set

backlog.spec: Create the Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator set to rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvPatterns (or equivalent feature invariants), radius 2, 2048 bits, and use it instead of the default atom invariants. Feature invariants group atoms by pharmacophore role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, etc.), which generalizes better across different scaffolds. Keep the RandomForest unchanged.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP-style) bits

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan features with count-based atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Fit the RandomForest on them. Atom pairs capture long-range topology and are complementary to circular fingerprints.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build Morgan count fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 with 1024 bits each, and concatenate them into one 3072-dimensional vector. Fit the RandomForest on this vector. Multiple radii give a range of substructure sizes that the single radius-2 fingerprint lacks.
backlog.title: Multi-radius hashed fingerprint

backlog.spec: In featurize, preprocess each molecule before fingerprinting: remove salts and small counter-ions with rdkit.Chem.SaltRemover or by keeping the largest fragment (split on '.' and keep the heaviest part), neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and fall back to the original molecule if parsing fails. Clean inputs reduce noise from salt forms and charged states.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurization

backlog.spec: Set class_weight='balanced_subsample' in the RandomForestClassifier. Keep all other settings the same. This reweights the classes so the forest is not biased toward the majority label; AUROC may benefit from better minority-class ranking.
backlog.title: Class-balanced random forest

backlog.spec: Change the RandomForest to max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=2 and max_depth=None, with n_estimators=500. Using sqrt(2048) features per split instead of 0.3 decorrelates trees more strongly, and a slightly larger leaf size smooths the probability estimates.
backlog.title: Tuned RandomForest regularization

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestClassifier with ExtraTreesClassifier (n_estimators=500, max_features='sqrt', min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed) on the same Morgan bit features. Extremely randomized split thresholds add more diversity and often give smoother probability rankings on fingerprint data.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees instead of RandomForest

backlog.spec: Concatenate Morgan count fingerprints with the RDKit 2D descriptors and fit a LightGBM classifier (objective binary, n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8, bagging_freq=1, min_child_samples=10, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8). Gradient-boosted trees often beat random forests on tabular molecular features.
backlog.title: LightGBM on fingerprint and descriptor features

backlog.spec: Fit an XGBClassifier on Morgan count fingerprints (2048 bits) with n_estimators=400, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.3, min_child_weight=2, tree_method='hist', random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Return predict_proba for class 1.
backlog.title: XGBoost on fingerprint features

backlog.spec: Concatenate the Morgan bits with the RDKit 2D descriptors and fit a CatBoostClassifier (iterations=600, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, l2_leaf_reg=3, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8). CatBoost's ordered boosting is often robust with small, noisy datasets.
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors and fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute the RDKit 2D descriptors, replace NaN and inf with 0, clip to training-set percentiles, standardize with StandardScaler fitted on the training fold, and fit LogisticRegression(C=0.1, max_iter=2000, random_state=seed). A linear model on physicochemical descriptors is a strong, low-variance baseline for BBB penetration.
backlog.title: Logistic regression on physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto (Jaccard) similarity matrix between Morgan bit fingerprints (for binary vectors: sum of min over sum of max, or AND-count / (a+b-AND-count)). Fit sklearn SVC(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, probability=True, random_state=seed) on the train-train kernel and predict with the test-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular activity prediction.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVM

backlog.spec: Compute Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules on Morgan bit fingerprints. For each test molecule, take the k=15 most similar training molecules and return the similarity-weighted mean of their labels (weights = similarity to the power 3). This instance-based method is cheap and captures local structure-activity similarity.
backlog.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour vote

backlog.spec: Train three models on the same training fold: the RandomForest on Morgan bits, a LightGBM on Morgan bits plus descriptors, and a logistic regression on standardized descriptors. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks scaled to [0,1] with scipy.stats.rankdata, and average the three rank vectors with equal weight. Since the metric is AUROC, rank averaging avoids miscalibration issues between models.
backlog.title: Rank-average ensemble of RF, LightGBM and logistic regression

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, split the training data into 5 stratified folds (seeded). For each fold, train a RandomForest and a LightGBM on the other four folds, and collect out-of-fold predictions for the held-out fold. Stack the two out-of-fold prediction columns and fit a LogisticRegression meta-model on them. For the test set, average the base models trained on the full training data and apply the meta-model. This learns the best weighting of base models from data.
backlog.title: Stacking with inner out-of-fold meta-model

backlog.spec: Use sklearn MLPClassifier with hidden_layer_sizes=(512, 128), alpha=1e-3 (L2), learning_rate_init=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction=0.15, n_iter_no_change=15, max_iter=300, random_state=seed, on the Morgan bit vectors. Early stopping on a held-out slice of the training fold controls overfitting in the network.
backlog.title: MLP on fingerprint bits with dropout-like early stopping

backlog.spec: Fit LightGBM with a lower learning rate (0.02) and up to 2000 rounds. Carve out a stratified 15% validation split of the training fold (seeded), use early_stopping(100) on it to choose the number of rounds, then retrain on the full training fold using the best iteration count (scaled by 1.1). Automatic round selection avoids both underfitting and overfitting.
backlog.title: LightGBM with learning-rate schedule and early stopping

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with a learning-rate schedule via the callbacks argument: reset_parameter with learning_rate decaying linearly from 0.1 to 0.01 over 800 rounds. Set num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=20, feature_fraction=0.3, bagging_fraction=0.8. Large early steps followed by fine adjustments often improve the boosting fit on small noisy datasets.
backlog.title: Decaying shrinkage gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models on the Morgan count plus descriptor features, each with a different random seed derived from the seed argument (seed*10+i), using bagging_fraction=0.7 and feature_fraction=0.3, and average their predicted probabilities. Averaging over bagged seeds reduces the variance of boosted trees.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged bagging of gradient-boosted models

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffolds for training molecules. For each of 20 bagging rounds, sample scaffold groups with replacement (rather than individual molecules), gather all molecules from the sampled groups, fit a RandomForest with 100 trees on them, and average the test predictions across rounds. Resampling by scaffold mirrors the scaffold split used in evaluation and avoids over-trusting near-duplicate scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware bootstrap bagging

backlog.spec: For each training molecule, generate 4 randomized SMILES using Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False) with a random generator seeded from the seed argument, keeping the original label, and augment the training set with these strings. At test time, produce 8 randomized SMILES per test molecule, compute predictions for each, and average the probabilities. This gives the model multiple views of each molecule's structure.
backlog.title: Randomized SMILES augmentation with test-time averaging

backlog.spec: Compute the classical BBB heuristic terms for each molecule: TPSA, molecular weight, number of H-bond donors, and a charge indicator (for acids, count of carboxylic acid and tetrazole groups). Append these scaled values, plus a rule score counting how many of the Lipinski-like thresholds (TPSA<90, MW<450, HBD<=3, no acid groups) are satisfied, to the Morgan bits. Fit the RandomForest on this augmented feature set. The explicit rule score gives the trees a direct signal they would otherwise need many splits to find.
backlog.title: Physicochemical BBB rule prior as an extra feature

backlog.spec: Keep the current featurize() unchanged. In fit_predict, replace LGBMClassifier with lightgbm.LGBMRanker(objective='lambdarank', n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, min_child_samples=10, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed). Fit it on all training rows as one query group (group=[len(train_y)]) with the 0/1 labels as relevance. Because the metric is AUROC, a pairwise ranking loss targets the same quantity directly. Return the ranker's raw scores passed through a sigmoid so the output is in [0,1] and the values are still usable as probabilities of class 1 for the harness.
backlog.title: LambdaRank pairwise objective for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Keep the Morgan count features and RDKit descriptors. In fit_predict, build a monotone_constraints list of length equal to the feature count: 0 for all Morgan bit columns, and for the descriptor columns set +1 for MolWt, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors... no, use the signs that are known to lower BBB penetration: -1 for TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, and +1 for MolLogP. Look up these columns by name using the index of Descriptors.descList. Pass monotone_constraints=that list and monotone_constraints_method='advanced' to LGBMClassifier. The constraint is a strong regularizer that should help generalization across unseen scaffolds, since the physics-based trends transfer across chemotypes.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on physicochemical descriptors

backlog.spec: Keep featurize() and the LightGBM classifier unchanged. In fit_predict, compute the Bemis-Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, includeChirality=False) of each training molecule. Count how many training molecules share each scaffold, and set each molecule's sample weight to 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold). Normalize the weights so their mean is 1. Pass them as sample_weight to model.fit. This stops large scaffold families (for example, many benzene-based compounds) from dominating the fit, so the trees learn chemotypes more evenly, which matches the evaluation on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-frequency sample weighting

backlog.spec: Keep the existing LightGBM model and featurization. Add a second, separate predictor: a Laplacian-corrected Bayesian classifier over binary ECFP4 bits (radius 2, 2048 bits, fingerprint turned into presence/absence). For each bit, compute the active-class frequency among training molecules with that bit on, p_b = (n_active_with_bit + 1) / (n_with_bit + 2) normalized as in Pipeline-Pilot-style Laplacian correction, and form a per-molecule score as the sum over present bits of log(p_b/p_prior) plus the same for absent bits. Convert to a probability with a sigmoid. Rank-average this score with the LightGBM probability at equal weight, using the rank of each prediction within the test set. The Bayesian model is very different from trees and is known to work well on BBB-type data.
backlog.title: Laplacian-corrected naive Bayes on Morgan bits, rank-blended with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Keep featurize() and the LightGBM classifier. In fit_predict, first fit the model on the training molecules and predict the test molecules. Take the test molecules with predicted probability above 0.85 as pseudo-class 1 and those below 0.15 as pseudo-class 0, and add them to the training set with weight 0.5 (use sample_weight). Refit the model with the same seed and return its predictions on the test molecules. Only one round is used. Since the test molecules come from the harness's unseen scaffolds, this lets the model adapt to the local chemistry of the test fold without using any labels from it.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-labelling on the test molecules

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Morgan count and RDKit descriptor features, and add a small block of 3D shape features. For each molecule, use Chem.AddHs, AllChem.EmbedMolecule with randomSeed=seed-independent fixed value 42 (ETKDGv3, maxAttempts=5), and if the embedding succeeds, compute rdMolDescriptors.CalcPBF, CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2, CalcRadiusOfGyration, CalcPMI1, CalcPMI2, CalcPMI3, and CalcSpherocityIndex. Use -1 for molecules whose embedding fails. Hydrogens are removed before the descriptor calculation. Append these 8 values to the feature matrix. Shape and molecular flatness are plausibly linked to membrane permeation beyond what 2D descriptors capture.
backlog.title: 3D shape descriptors from a single ETKDG conformer

backlog.spec: Keep featurize() unchanged. In fit_predict, change the LightGBM settings to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, max_drop=50, learning_rate=0.1, n_estimators=300, num_leaves=31, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, min_child_samples=10, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed. DART randomly drops previously added trees during each boosting round, which reduces over-specialization of later trees and acts as a regularizer. Only these settings change. Keep the rest of the script the same.
backlog.title: DART boosting (dropout trees) for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Keep featurize() and the LightGBM settings unchanged. In fit_predict, build 10 bags. For bag k, draw all training molecules of the minority class and an equal-sized random subsample (with replacement=False, seeded by seed*100+k via numpy default_rng) of the majority class. Fit a LightGBM classifier with random_state=seed*100+k on each bag, and average the predict_proba outputs over the 10 bags for the test molecules. Undersampling gives each tree a balanced view of the two classes, and the averaging over bags recovers the information lost by discarding majority rows.
backlog.title: Balanced undersampling bagging ensemble

backlog.spec: Keep featurize() and the LightGBM classifier settings unchanged, with n_estimators=400. After fitting, do not use the final model only. Instead, for num_iteration in [100, 200, 300, 400], call model.predict_proba(X_test, num_iteration=num_iteration)[:, 1] and average the four probability vectors with equal weight. The early snapshots are less overfit and the late ones are more fitted. Averaging them gives a smoother, lower-variance ranking at no extra training cost.
backlog.title: Snapshot averaging across boosting iterations

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Morgan count and RDKit descriptor features, and add a small block of electronic features. For each molecule, call rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges(mol) (from rdkit.Chem.rdPartialCharges), read the atomic partial charges, and compute, over heavy atoms: the maximum charge, the minimum charge, the sum of absolute charges, the sum of positive charges, the sum of negative charges, and the charge of the most polar heteroatom (N or O). Replace NaN and inf values with 0. Append these 6 numbers to the feature matrix. Partial charge distribution is closely tied to the desolvation cost of crossing a lipid membrane, which is a core determinant of BBB penetration.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge statistics as descriptors

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, define 3 LightGBM configurations that differ in capacity: num_leaves 7 with min_child_samples 20, num_leaves 15 with min_child_samples 10, and num_leaves 31 with min_child_samples 10 (keep learning_rate 0.05, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.8). Split the training molecules with a 4-fold GroupKFold, grouping by RDKit Murcko scaffold, and score each configuration by inner out-of-fold ROC AUC. Refit the best configuration on all training molecules with random_state=seed and return its test probabilities. Keep the featurize() call computed once and reuse the matrix across inner folds so the job stays under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Inner-CV selection among LightGBM configurations

backlog.spec: Append a small block of ionization-related counts to the existing featurize() output. Using RDKit SMARTS patterns, count carboxylic acids and their conjugate bases, tetrazoles, acyl sulfonamides, aliphatic primary, secondary and tertiary amines, amidines and guanidines, quaternary ammonium nitrogens, and phenolic hydroxyls. Also add a binary flag for net formal charge being nonzero. These are about 10 extra float features, so the rest of the pipeline (LightGBM, same hyperparameters) is unchanged. The rationale is that acids and permanently charged groups reduce passive BBB penetration in a way raw Morgan bits capture only weakly.
backlog.title: Ionization-state SMARTS counts as features

backlog.spec: Before fitting, drop every feature column whose value is constant across the training matrix, computed inside fit_predict on train rows only, and apply the same column mask to the test matrix. Then set LightGBM's extra_trees=True, which draws one random threshold per feature per split, as a regularizer. Keep the other hyperparameters as in the current file but raise n_estimators to 600 because extra random splits learn more slowly. Use random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Extremely randomized LightGBM splits with constant-column pruning

backlog.spec: Replace the hard 0/1 training labels with smoothed targets: positives become 0.95 and negatives 0.05. LightGBM's binary objective does not accept soft labels directly, so instead duplicate each training row, keep one copy labelled 1 with weight 0.95 and one copy labelled 0 with weight 0.95, and add a second copy of the opposite label with weight 0.05. Equivalently, use a cross-entropy objective through LGBMClassifier sample weights. Keep all other settings unchanged. The aim is to reduce overconfident leaves on the noisy borderline molecules.
backlog.title: Soft-label smoothing for the binary targets

backlog.spec: Fit a TruncatedSVD with 64 components on the count Morgan fingerprint matrix of the union of training and test molecules (no labels are used, so this is transductive but label-free). Append the 64 component scores to the existing feature matrix before LightGBM. Use random_state=seed for the SVD. The embedding gives the trees smooth, dense directions that summarize co-occurring substructures, which sparse bits cannot provide. Keep all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Unsupervised SVD embedding of count fingerprints

backlog.spec: For each molecule compute, from Tanimoto similarities on binary ECFP4 bits, the maximum similarity to training positives and the maximum similarity to training negatives, and append both, plus their difference, as features for LightGBM. For training rows these features must be computed out-of-fold: split the training molecules into 5 GroupKFold groups by Murcko scaffold, and for each training row compute similarities only against the other folds. For test rows use all training molecules. Use RDKit BulkTanimotoSimilarity or numpy bit-matrix arithmetic. This turns similarity-based evidence into inputs that trees can combine with the physicochemical descriptors.
backlog.title: Nearest-positive and nearest-negative similarity features

backlog.spec: Keep LightGBM and its current hyperparameters, but change colsample_bytree over the boosting rounds instead of fixing it at 0.3. Use LightGBM's callback reset_parameter with a schedule that starts at feature_fraction 0.1 for the first 100 rounds and rises linearly to 0.5 at round 400, so early trees are forced to use diverse, sparse substructures and later trees can use the strong descriptors. Keep learning_rate 0.05 and n_estimators 400, and use random_state=seed.
backlog.title: Annealed feature-fraction schedule during boosting

backlog.spec: Train 6 LightGBM models, each on a different random 50 percent subset of the feature columns drawn with numpy's RandomState(seed + k) for model index k, and each using all training rows. Set colsample_bytree to 1.0 inside each model, since the subspace is already fixed. Average their test probabilities with equal weight and return the mean. Keep the other LightGBM hyperparameters unchanged. This random-subspace idea differs from seed averaging, because each member sees a structurally different view of the descriptors and fingerprint bits.
backlog.title: Random-subspace bagging of LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace LightGBM with a small multilayer perceptron implemented in scikit-learn or with numpy: compute the RDKit descriptor block and the binary Morgan bits, apply sklearn QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on training rows only, then train an MLP with hidden layers of 256 and 64 units, ReLU, dropout-like early stopping on a 10 percent validation split of the training molecules, and L2 weight decay alpha=1e-3. Use the Adam optimizer with learning rate 1e-3 and batch size 64, and average the predictions of the last 5 epochs as a snapshot ensemble. Set all random states to seed. Keep training time under the 10 minute job limit by capping epochs at 60.
backlog.title: Standardized MLP on quantile-transformed descriptors

backlog.spec: Append a small set of ring-topology features to the existing feature matrix. Using RDKit, compute the number of ring systems (fused ring clusters), the size of the largest ring system in heavy atoms, the number of aromatic rings, the number of non-aromatic rings, the fraction of sp3 carbons, the number of stereocentres, the number of rotatable bonds, and the ratio of heavy atoms to ring atoms. Do not use scaffold identity hashes, since scaffolds are unseen across folds by design. These roughly 8 features summarize the three-dimensional rigidity and planarity that govern membrane crossing, and LightGBM is kept as the model.
backlog.title: Ring-system and shape-count descriptors

backlog.spec: In featurize(), add a count vector over BRICS fragments. For each molecule call rdkit.Chem.BRICS.BRICSDecompose(mol) to get the set of fragment SMILES strings. Build a vocabulary from the training molecules only, keeping fragments that occur in at least 5 training molecules, and cap it at 512 columns. For each molecule, count how many times each kept fragment occurs, or use the presence/absence of each one, and append these columns to the existing Morgan count and descriptor matrix. Fragments not in the vocabulary are ignored. Build the vocabulary inside fit_predict, not at module level, so no test information leaks into training. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: BRICS fragment count features

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan count block with a graph-propagated atom feature block. For each molecule, build a per-atom vector from atomic number one-hot (common elements), degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count, and ring membership. Propagate it over the bond graph without any learned weights: for hops k = 0, 1, 2, 3, average each atom's vector with its neighbours (self-loops included) and then sum over atoms. Concatenate the 4 pooled vectors (sum and mean per hop) into one dense feature vector per molecule, append it to the existing descriptor features, and keep the LightGBM model unchanged. This is a parameter-free SGC-style feature extractor, so the fit stays a single LightGBM call.
backlog.title: Hop-wise atom-feature propagation (training-free graph convolution)

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute ECFP4 bit vectors for the training and test molecules together. Build a sparse kNN graph (k = 10) with Tanimoto similarity, using only the bits, and symmetrise it. Run label spreading (Zhou-style iteration F <- alpha*S*F + (1-alpha)*Y, alpha = 0.8, 30 iterations, S = normalised adjacency) with the training labels clamped and the test rows starting at 0. Take the converged score for each test molecule and the same score for each training molecule computed out-of-fold (5 inner folds, labels hidden for the held-out rows). Append this spread score as one extra column for LightGBM. Use the seed for any fold split. Keep it self-contained inside fit_predict.
backlog.title: Transductive label spreading over the train+test Tanimoto graph

backlog.spec: Compute ring-system strings for every molecule. Take each ring system as the set of fused or linked rings, ignoring side chains, using the Murcko scaffold with the side chains removed, or rdkit ring info. Inside fit_predict, compute the training positive rate for each ring-system string, smoothed toward the global positive rate with m = 10 pseudo-counts. Use out-of-fold encoding on the training rows (5 inner folds) so that a molecule never sees its own label. For test molecules, use the full-training encoding, and assign the global rate to unseen ring systems. Append the encoded value, together with the number of molecules that share the ring system, as two extra LightGBM features. Keep the existing features unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-smoothed target encoding of ring systems

backlog.spec: Keep the feature set unchanged and change only the LightGBM hyperparameters to a regularised regime: num_leaves=7, max_depth=3, n_estimators=1200, learning_rate=0.03, min_child_samples=30, reg_lambda=5.0, reg_alpha=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7 with subsample_freq=1, and min_split_gain=0.01. Use the same seed argument for random_state. The aim is a smoother, lower-variance function that generalises across unseen scaffolds, since the current 31-leaf trees may overfit to scaffold-specific bits.
backlog.title: Shallow, strongly regularised LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before fitting LightGBM, build an augmented training set. Draw a number of pairs equal to the number of training rows, using a seeded RNG. For each pair (i, j), sample lambda from Beta(0.4, 0.4), and create x = lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j and y = lambda*y_i + (1-lambda)*y_j. Concatenate the originals and the mixed rows, so the target is a soft label in [0, 1]. Fit LightGBM with objective='cross_entropy' (xentropy), which accepts soft labels, and keep the other hyperparameters the same. Predict on the unmodified test features. Use only the seed argument for randomness.
backlog.title: Feature-space mixup augmentation for boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the built-in binary objective with a custom focal-style objective passed to LightGBM as the objective callable. Use gamma = 1.5, with alpha = 0.5 so that the classes are not reweighted. The gradient and hessian are computed from the sigmoid of the raw score: p = sigmoid(f), with the usual focal-loss derivatives for the positive and negative classes. Clip the hessian below at 1e-6. Keep the number of estimators, learning rate, and other hyperparameters the same. In predict, apply sigmoid to the raw score so the returned values are probabilities of class 1. The idea is to concentrate the boosting on the hard, mislabeled-looking molecules near the decision boundary, which is where AUROC is decided.
backlog.title: Focal-loss custom objective for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first fit a LightGBM model on the full feature set (current settings, seed passed through). Read its split-gain feature importances, keep the top 300 columns by total gain, and then refit a second LightGBM model with the same hyperparameters on only those columns. Use the importances from training data only, so no test molecule is involved in the selection. Predict on the test features with the same kept columns. This is a one-level embedded feature selection that drops the many near-useless Morgan bits and some descriptors, which may reduce overfitting to scaffold-specific bits.
backlog.title: Gain-based two-stage feature pruning

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 3 rounds of re-weighting. In round 0, fit LightGBM with uniform weights on the training rows. Compute out-of-fold predicted probabilities on the training rows with 4 inner stratified folds. Give each training row a weight equal to 1 if its out-of-fold log loss is below the median, and 0.3 otherwise. In rounds 1 and 2, refit on the training rows with these weights and recompute the out-of-fold losses the same way. The final model is trained on all training rows with the weights from the last round and predicts the test rows. Inner folds and the seed are the only sources of randomness. The aim is to down-weight label-noisy or atypical molecules that hurt the ranking.
backlog.title: Self-paced sample reweighting by out-of-fold loss

backlog.spec: Add the extended reduced-graph fingerprint from rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint(mol) as an extra dense feature block. It is a 315-dimensional float vector that encodes pharmacophoric pair distances between donor, acceptor, aromatic, and charged groups. Compute it for every molecule in featurize() and append it to the existing count-Morgan and descriptor matrix. Keep all LightGBM settings unchanged. Wrap the call in a try/except that falls back to a zero vector for molecules where it fails, so that no fold crashes.
backlog.title: Pharmacophore reduced-graph (ErG) fingerprint features

backlog.spec: Keep the current featurize() but append a bag of SMILES character n-grams instead of relying only on graph fingerprints. Inside fit_predict, build a CountVectorizer(analyzer='char', ngram_range=(2,6), min_df=5, lowercase=False) fitted on train_smiles only, and transform both train and test. Cap the vocabulary at about 1000 columns (max_features=1000) and hstack the sparse counts with the existing float32 matrix before LightGBM. Fitting the vectorizer on training rows only keeps every fold leak-free. Everything else (LightGBM settings, seed use) stays the same.
backlog.title: SMILES character n-gram count features

backlog.spec: Extend featurize() by appending two RDKit descriptor families the file does not yet use: the 42 molecular quantum numbers from rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_(m) and the EState atom-type counts from EState.EState.EStateIndices summed per atom type (use fixed-length vectors, pad with zeros). Compute them per molecule, replace NaN or inf with 0, and clip to +/-1e6 as the current code does. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Test whether the extra physchem-like counts help the trees separate the classes.
backlog.title: MQN and EState count descriptors appended

backlog.spec: Add a label-independent density feature for each molecule. Inside fit_predict, compute the Tanimoto similarity (on Morgan bit vectors, radius 2, 2048 bits) of every training molecule to every other training molecule, and of every test molecule to the training set. For each molecule record the mean similarity to its k=5 and k=20 nearest training neighbours, excluding itself on the training side. Append these two columns to the feature matrix. They tell the model how typical a molecule is for the training distribution, without using labels, so there is no leakage.
backlog.title: Label-free kNN density features

backlog.spec: Remove likely mislabelled training molecules before the final fit. Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold StratifiedKFold (shuffled, random_state=seed) on the training rows with the current LightGBM to get out-of-fold probabilities. Drop training rows whose given label is the opposite of the OOF prediction and whose confidence exceeds 0.8 (for example, label 1 with OOF probability below 0.2). Then train the usual LightGBM on the cleaned rows and predict the test molecules. Test molecules are never touched during cleaning.
backlog.title: Confident-learning label cleaning

backlog.spec: After the LightGBM predicts probabilities for the test molecules, smooth them over the test-test similarity graph. Compute Tanimoto similarity between test molecules on Morgan radius-2 bit vectors, keep the k=5 nearest test neighbours of each molecule with similarity above 0.4, and replace each prediction with 0.5 * own prediction + 0.5 * mean of its kept neighbours' predictions (leave the prediction unchanged if no neighbour passes the threshold). Use only the test inputs, never their labels, so the smoothing is legal in the harness. Clip the result to [0,1].
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions

backlog.spec: Set linear_tree=True in the LGBMClassifier, with linear_lambda=1.0, and keep the rest of the current settings. Linear-leaf trees fit a small ridge model in each leaf rather than a constant, which can capture smooth trends in the descriptor columns (molecular weight, logP, TPSA) that axis-aligned splits approximate poorly. Standardize the descriptor columns with the training means and standard deviations before fitting, because linear leaves are sensitive to scale, and clip after standardization to [-10, 10]. Fingerprint counts can remain unscaled.
backlog.title: LightGBM with linear leaves

backlog.spec: Replace the tree model with a tiny graph neural network written in plain numpy. For each molecule build atom features (element one-hot for common elements, degree, formal charge, aromaticity, H count, ring membership) and the bond adjacency. Run 3 rounds of message passing where each atom sums neighbour states through a shared weight matrix (hidden size 64) with tanh, then sum-pool to a molecule vector and apply a linear output with sigmoid. Train full-batch with Adam (lr 0.01, weight decay 1e-4) for about 200 epochs using binary cross-entropy, with the gradients written out by hand or via a small autograd-free backprop. Average 3 seeds for the test predictions. Keep the code short and check that the job stays within the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Bold: small message-passing network in numpy

backlog.spec: Replace the LightGBM predictor with kernel ridge regression on the labels, using a Tanimoto kernel K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b)) / sum(max(a,b)) over count Morgan vectors (radius 2). Fit alpha = solve(K_train + lambda I, y_train_pm) with y in {-1,+1} and lambda around 1.0, then predict the test molecules as K_test @ alpha, and map the output to (0,1) with a logistic function so the returned values are probabilities. Grid-search lambda over {0.1, 1, 10} with an inner 3-fold scaffold-grouped split on the training rows (group by Murcko scaffold). The point is to test whether a similarity-based kernel model captures BBB patterns that trees miss.
backlog.title: Bold: Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process classifier as the predictor

backlog.spec: Keep the current LightGBM model but adjust two regularity knobs within a narrow range: set colsample_bynode=0.5 in addition to colsample_bytree=0.3 (per-node feature subsampling) and raise min_child_samples from 10 to 20. Also set max_bin=127 to reduce binning noise in the sparse count columns. Do not change the learning rate, the tree count, or num_leaves. This tests whether a small change in tree diversity helps while avoiding the heavy regularization that already hurt.
backlog.title: Mild LightGBM column and leaf tuning

backlog.spec: In featurize, replace the hashed 2048-bit Morgan count vector with an unfolded vocabulary built inside fit_predict from the training molecules only. Use rdFingerprintGenerator with fpSize large (e.g. 2**20) and collect the sparse count dict per molecule via GetSparseCountFingerprint, keep only substructure IDs that occur in at least 5 training molecules, and map them to dense columns. Test molecules use the same vocabulary, and IDs not in it are dropped. Concatenate with the existing RDKit descriptors and keep the LightGBM settings unchanged. This removes hash collisions while keeping the feature set finite.
backlog.title: Unfolded sparse Morgan vocabulary instead of hashing

backlog.spec: Keep the current Morgan count plus descriptor matrix and append two more fixed-length fingerprints computed on each molecule: rdkit.Chem.RDKFingerprint (path-based, fpSize=1024, maxPath=5) and rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP (nBits=1024). Both are deterministic and need no fitting, so featurize simply hstacks them. Leave the LightGBM model, colsample_bytree=0.3, and the seed handling unchanged. The aim is to add path-based substructure information that Morgan bits do not capture.
backlog.title: Append RDKit path-based and Avalon fingerprints

backlog.spec: Before featurization in fit_predict, canonicalize each training SMILES with Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and group identical canonical strings. For each group, keep one row whose label is the mean of the group's labels, and then round to 0 or 1 only when the mean is exactly 0 or 1, otherwise keep the soft mean as a sample weight of the group size. Train LightGBM on the deduplicated rows, with sample_weight equal to the group size. Predict test molecules as usual. The change removes duplicated copies that otherwise get over-counted.
backlog.title: Deduplicate canonical structures and average labels

backlog.spec: Before training, produce K=10 bootstrap-sampled copies of the standardized descriptor block (use the seed argument). For each copy, split the descriptor columns into random subsets of 8 columns, run PCA with whitening on each subset using the training rows only, and project the training and test rows onto those components. Concatenate all projected components with the original feature matrix (Morgan counts plus descriptors) and fit the existing LightGBM model on the augmented matrix. The oblique rotations give the trees linear combinations of physicochemical properties they cannot form by axis-aligned splits.
backlog.title: Rotation-forest style oblique projections for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Split the training set at the median molecular weight (Descriptors.MolWt, computed from the existing descriptor block) into a small-molecule group and a large-molecule group. Fit one LightGBM model per group using the existing feature matrix and settings, with each group fitting only its own rows. For a test molecule, compute its MolWt and pick the expert for its side of the split, with a soft blend in a window of plus or minus 25 Da around the median where the two experts' predictions are averaged. Return the blended probabilities. This lets each expert specialise in the chemistry typical of its size range.
backlog.title: Size-gated mixture of two experts

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, pick four physicochemical columns from the descriptor block that are known to relate to BBB penetration: TPSA, MolWt, MolLogP, and NumHDonors. For each of them, fit an out-of-fold LightGBMRegressor on the Morgan count features with 5 inner folds (using the seed), and produce out-of-fold predictions on the training rows and full-fit predictions on the test rows. Append these four predicted values as extra columns to the feature matrix and train the existing LightGBM classifier on the augmented matrix. The auxiliary targets are continuous and carry richer signal than the binary label alone.
backlog.title: Auxiliary physicochemical regression stacking

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replicate the training matrix 3 times. For the continuous descriptor columns only, add Gaussian noise to the copies with standard deviation equal to 0.05 times each column's training-set standard deviation, and leave the Morgan count columns untouched. Stack the original and noisy copies (with the same labels), and fit the existing LightGBM model on the stacked data with min_child_samples scaled up by 3 to keep the leaf sizes comparable. Predict test molecules on clean features. The noise acts as a smoothing regulariser that discourages the trees from splitting on tiny descriptor differences.
backlog.title: Gaussian input-noise augmentation with replicated rows

backlog.spec: Train in two stages inside fit_predict. Stage one fits a shallow LightGBM with num_leaves=7, learning_rate=0.05 and 150 trees on the training matrix. Stage two uses the raw margin predictions of stage one on the training rows as init_score and fits the existing 31-leaf LightGBM for 400 trees with the same settings. For test molecules, compute the stage-one raw margin, add the stage-two raw_score output, and convert with the sigmoid function. The schedule grows tree complexity gradually, so the coarse structure is learned before finer interactions are added.
backlog.title: Complexity curriculum via init_score chaining

backlog.spec: Fit the existing LightGBM model once on the full feature matrix within fit_predict and read the feature_importances_ with importance_type='gain'. Take the 15 descriptor columns with the highest gain (only from the RDKit descriptor block, not the Morgan bits). Build all pairwise products and pairwise differences of their standardized values, using standardization parameters from the training rows only, and append them as new columns. Refit the same LightGBM on the extended matrix. The explicit interactions, such as polarity times size, are the kind of combined physicochemical signal that BBB rules encode.
backlog.title: Pairwise products of top-gain descriptors

backlog.spec: Change only the LGBMClassifier settings: set is_unbalance=True, or equivalently scale_pos_weight equal to the ratio of negative to positive training labels computed inside fit_predict. This reweights the binary logloss so that the minority class contributes equally to the gradient. Keep all other hyperparameters, the featurization, and seed handling unchanged. Because AUROC depends only on ranking, the reweighting changes the tree structure and the relative order of the scores, which can shift the ranking across the scaffold folds.
backlog.title: Class-balanced LightGBM loss with is_unbalance

backlog.spec: In featurize(), for each molecule call rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs(mol) to get the per-heavy-atom (logP, MR) contributions. Bin the logP contributions into 8 fixed bins over [-1, 1] and the MR contributions into 8 fixed bins over [-5, 15] (values clipped into the end bins), and count atoms per bin. Append the 16 counts plus the fraction of atoms with positive logP contribution to the existing feature vector. Fixed bin edges mean no fitting is needed, so the features are label-free and identical for train and test. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-atom Crippen contribution histograms

backlog.spec: In featurize(), append RDKit's 2D autocorrelation descriptor vector rdMolDescriptors.CalcAUTOCORR2D(mol), which gives 192 topological autocorrelation values over several atomic properties (mass, charge, polarizability, Crippen logP and MR, etc.). Compute it per molecule, replace any NaN with 0, and hstack it after the existing Morgan count and RDKit descriptor columns. No fitting is involved. Leave LightGBM settings unchanged. The aim is a compact, property-weighted topological description that the bit-hashed Morgan vector does not capture.
backlog.title: 2D autocorrelation descriptors appended

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, for the training rows only, compute a naive-Bayes-style log-odds per radius-2 Morgan bit: for each bit set in the training molecules, encode it as log((pos + 1) / (neg + 1)) using counts that are smoothed toward the base rate with m = 10 pseudo-counts. To avoid target leakage, build these encodings out-of-fold (5 inner stratified folds on the training rows), and for test rows use encodings from all training rows. Append the per-molecule mean and max of the encodings over that molecule's set bits (2 numbers) to the existing LightGBM features. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold smoothed log-odds encoding of Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Before computing fingerprints and descriptors, pass each molecule through rdMolStandardize.TautomerEnumerator (default settings, with a fixed max-tautomer cap) and use its Canonicalize() output as the molecule for featurize(). Fall back to the original molecule if canonicalization raises an exception or returns None. This is applied to both training and test SMILES identically, uses no labels, and changes only the input representation of molecules whose tautomer form varies, which is common among amines, amides and heteroaromatic NH compounds. Leave the model settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Tautomer canonicalisation before featurization

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity between training molecules (BulkTanimotoSimilarity on binary Morgan fingerprints). For each training molecule count the training molecules with similarity >= 0.6 (including itself). Set its sample weight to 1 / count, then normalise the weights to have mean 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to LGBMClassifier.fit. This down-weights over-represented chemical series so the model is not dominated by large clusters. Test molecules are not used. The test-time features and predict call are unchanged.
backlog.title: Inverse-density sample weights from Tanimoto neighbourhoods

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, cluster the training molecules with Butina clustering on ECFP4 Tanimoto distances at a 0.6 distance cutoff (rdkit.ML.Cluster.Butina). Build 5 bags, where each bag randomly drops about 20 percent of the clusters (whole clusters, not individual molecules), using a RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Fit one LightGBM per bag with the same settings, using a different random_state per bag. Average their predict_proba outputs on the test molecules. Cluster-level dropping makes each bag miss whole chemical series, which matches the scaffold-held-out evaluation better than row bootstrap.
backlog.title: Butina-cluster drop bagging

backlog.spec: Replace the 31-leaf LightGBM with an additive model: LGBMClassifier with num_leaves=2 (depth-one stumps), learning_rate 0.1, around 1500 boosting rounds, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample 0.8, and min_child_samples 20. Stumps with no interactions give a generalized additive model over the Morgan counts and descriptors, which is a different inductive bias from the current deep trees. Keep the features and the seed handling unchanged. Use a seeded inner 5-fold early-stopping check on the training rows to pick the number of rounds once, and reuse it for the final fit.
backlog.title: Stump-based additive boosting (EBM-style GAM)

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train a sklearn RandomForestClassifier (500 trees, max_features sqrt, min_samples_leaf 1, random_state=seed) on the training features, using 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on the training rows to get honest teacher probabilities. Then train the LightGBM student on a blend of the hard labels and the teacher probabilities: target = 0.5 * y + 0.5 * p_teacher. LightGBM's binary objective accepts soft labels in [0,1] via the cross-entropy objective ('cross_entropy'), so set objective='cross_entropy' and pass the blended targets. The teacher is used only inside fit_predict and only on the training rows, so no test leakage occurs.
backlog.title: Distilling out-of-fold random-forest probabilities as soft targets

backlog.spec: Keep LightGBM's subsample_freq=1, but replace the constant subsample=0.8 with a schedule that starts at 0.5 and rises linearly to 1.0 over the boosting rounds. Implement this by training in 4 consecutive chunks with continue training (init_model / or refitting with the booster's current predictions as init_score) of 100 rounds each, setting bagging_fraction to 0.5, 0.67, 0.83, 1.0 in turn, and reusing the same seeded RNG. Early boosting then explores with heavy row noise and late boosting refines on all rows. Leave the feature set, leaf count and learning rate unchanged.
backlog.title: Annealed row subsampling schedule

backlog.spec: Keep the current LightGBM setup (31 leaves, colsample_bytree 0.3, 400 trees) but set path_smooth=10 and min_sum_hessian_in_leaf=1.0. Path smoothing shrinks each leaf value toward its parent's value, which damps noisy leaves created from rare fingerprint bits without the strong global depth limits that already hurt in earlier runs. The change is two extra parameters on LGBMClassifier, so no other code changes are needed.
backlog.title: Path-smoothed leaf values as a regulariser

incumbent.description: Replace the random forest with a LightGBM binary classifier on concatenated Morgan count fingerprints (2048 bits, radius 2) and all RDKit 2D descriptors, using the specified hyperparameters.

memo: Helped: only slot 0, swapping random forest for LightGBM on Morgan counts plus descriptors (0.1361 to 0.0962). Nothing since has clearly beaten it. Noise sd is ~0.0049, so most single changes are within noise. Small gainers, all roughly within noise: ErG fingerprint 0.0915, nearest-positive/negative similarity features 0.0923, standardization 0.0925, atom-pair counts 0.0931, 6-model seed averaging 0.0932. Hurt: CatBoost 0.1074, shallow regularised LightGBM 0.1074, constant-column dropping 0.1046, stacking 0.1019, naive Bayes blend 0.1033, test-set smoothing 0.1035, decaying learning rate 0.1011. Many aborts were duplicates of features already in train.py, so read the file first. Next: combine the small gainers (ErG, similarity features, standardization, atom-pair counts, seed averaging) in one job, then replicate it to check whether the gains add up. Then try mild LightGBM tuning (column subsampling, min_child_samples). Avoid heavy regularization, model-family swaps and heterogeneous ensembles.
